en.title: The Old Rugged Cross
en.author: George Bennard
stanzas:
[A]On a hill far away stood an [D]old rugged cross,
[B7]The [E7]emblem of suff'ring and [A]shame;
[A]And I love that old cross where the [D]Dearest and Best
[B7]For a [E7]world of lost sinners was [A]slain.

Oh, that old rugged cross, so despised by the world,
Has a wondrous attraction for me;
For the dear Lamb of God left His glory above
To bear it to dark Calvary.

In that old rugged cross, stained with blood so divine,
A wondrous beauty I see,
For 'twas on that old cross Jesus suffered and died,
To pardon and sanctify me.
en.chorus:
[E7]So I'll cherish the old rugged [A]cross,
Till my [D]trophies at last I lay [A]down;
[A]I will cling to the old rugged [D]cross,
And ex[E7]change it someday for a [A]crown.

notes: Text from Timeless Truths (Evening Light Songs #511). Hymnary's representative text (United Methodist Hymnal) has the same four stanzas and differs only in 'suffering' for 'suff'ring', 'some day' as two words, lower-case 'dearest and best', and 'To that old rugged cross' for 'To the old rugged cross' in stanza 4; TT's readings kept. Tune OLD RUGGED CROSS, meter 12.8.12.8 with refrain per hymnary's text page (its tune record counts the half-lines as 6.6.8.6.6.8). Key: hymnary's instances run 60 B-flat to 4 A-flat and 2 A; TT prints B-flat. Moved to A for guitar per the key rule. Chords derived from the Timeless Truths MusicXML score by reading the four-part chord on every beat, transposed B-flat to A. Stanza: I for the first six syllables, IV on 'old rugged cross', the secondary dominant B (V of V) on the pickup word 'The' / 'For', then V7 and I; the diminished passing chords the inner voices make inside the I and IV bars were dropped. Refrain: V7 straight through 'cherish the old rugged' (a one-beat I under 'rug-' dropped), IV on 'trophies', the second half I-IV, then the cadential 6/4 under 'change' written as the E7 it resolves into. COPYRIGHT: words and music 1913, public domain in the United States; Bennard died 1958, so under life-plus-70 terms (Switzerland, the EU) the text is protected until the end of 2028.
